parsed.explanation: No trans-presenting crime is documented, but a visitor who is detained faces state-directed custody exposure: since 2022 mass raids capture trans women, ordinary prisons deny gender accommodation, and custody abuse includes forced shaving, punitive drills, denial of HIV care and sexual-assault risks; prison staff target effeminate men. Hospital care is discriminatory. Recourse is partial—one judge ordered release, another detainee remains imprisoned—while institutions repeatedly failed to address anti-LGBT violence. Positive hate-crime law and 2020 conviction of officers for killing a trans woman show some rule of law, but do not offset the hostile operating regime. Extreme social hostility (85% once said attacking trans people acceptable) compounds risk. High risk, below severe because no explicit visitor criminalisation, execution, or near-automatic prosecution is documented.
